subject: Maths
title: 4 times table
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (3, 4, 8 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall and use the 4 times table to multiply and divide.

key_vocab.definition: The 4 times table is a list of multiples of 4: numbers we get when we count in 4s. Multiples of 4 are always even, and you can find them by doubling the 2 times table.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall and use the 4 times table to multiply and divide.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 4 times table -- The 4 times table is a list of multiples of 4: numbers we get when we count in 4s. Multiples of 4 are always even, and you can find them by doubling the 2 times table.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. 4 × 4 means ‘4 groups of 4’. You can also think of it as ‘4 groups of 4’ — the answer is the same.
4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 4×4 = 16
Four groups of 4

Key examples:
  ✓ 1 × 4 = 4  (starting point)
  ✓ 2 × 4 = 8  (double)
  ✓ 5 × 4 = 20  (halfway to 10)
  ✗ 3 × 4 = 13  (wrong)
  ✗ 4 × 0 = 4  (any × 0 = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single multiplication
  Calculate 6 × 4
  6 groups of 4
  4 + 4 + 4 + 4  ...
  = 24
  = 24
  (Skip-count in 4s 6 times to reach 24.)

Example 2 – missing factor
  Solve: ___ × 4 = 20
  How many 4s in 20?
  Count up: 4, 8, 12, ...
  = 5
  = 5
  (Divide: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.)
